name: Meli 2009: burst-firing, stronger on the right, in dim red light
origin: Meli & Persinger 2009 (Behavioral Neuroscience Laboratory, Laurentian University)
summary: Thirty minutes of the lab's burst-firing pattern, stronger over the right temporal lobe, while you sit with your eyes open in dim red light. Meli & Persinger 2009 reported that the field raised a five-item 'presence' score (dizziness, sensed presence, detachment, ego-alien thoughts, being somewhere else) in red light and lowered it in white light, with no effect of the field on its own; 5 people per cell.
notes: 30 people in 6 cells (field or sham, in red, green or white light) wore the Koren helmet with four sets of solenoids. 'A burst-firing magnetic field, composed of 239 points, with point durations equal to 3 msec, was delivered once every 4 sec for 30 min (about 380 presentations)' (Meli 2009 p.3 [70]). 380 bursts in 30 min means a 4-s pause after each. The procedure 'was similar to' Persinger & Healey 2002, where each solenoid pair was on for 0.5 s (p.3 [535]). This program plays a 717-ms burst (239 points of 3 ms), then a 4-s pause. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: the paper says only that it was '2 uT higher over the right hemisphere compared to the left', with no absolute value or place (p.3 [70]). Here the left side plays at 0.4 of the right, this project's choice: at 1 uT the right is 0.6 uT higher, not 2 uT. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Result: the presence score was 6.6 with field against 1.4 with sham in red light, and 1.8 against 5.0 in white light; the field alone had no effect (p.3-4 [70-71]). 5 people per cell, one lab, not repeated elsewhere. This helmet has no light channel. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Seated with the eyes open in a quiet room lit only by dim red light. The study used two 40-watt bulbs covered with red gels, on stands about 1 m to the side; its comparison conditions were green and white light.
schedule: One 30-min session per condition. For a self-test, compare red with green or white light and field with sham (the app's Blind option) in blinded, counterbalanced sessions on different days, with the rating scale chosen in advance.
source: Meli & Persinger 2009, Red light facilitates the sensed presence elicited by application of weak, burst-firing magnetic fields over the temporal lobes, Int J Neurosci 119:68-75 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19116832/ ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2005, Int J Neurosci 115:1053-1079 (sensed presence and geomagnetic activity) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16051550/ ; Karbowski, Saroka, Murugan & Persinger 2015, Epilepsy Behav 51:127-132 (blue-light version) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26276250/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374-382 (burst-firing once every 3 s for about 0.7 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file, 3 ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Collins 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (3 ms points, 4 s between bursts) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/16d96136-680c-4afe-8044-f9137bd01afc ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
